Discovered from SA-0MSN2LIOQ004TON1 (discovered-from:SA-0MSN2LIOQ004TON1).

## Context
The committed, canonical pre-push hook is `.githooks/pre-push` v3 (worklog sync + branch policy + context-budget gate + scope-aware full-suite test gate). However, this clone's `git config core.hooksPath` is `.git/hooks`, and the active `.git/hooks/pre-push` is an uncommitted v2 (no `--repo-root` fix, no global-symlink fallback, no full-suite test gate). The v2 hook's context-budget gate still functions for SorraAgents because the local `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py` is present.

## Why this matters
- The active hook is uncommitted and can drift/disappear; the committed hook is not what runs.
- The v2 context gate lacks the `--repo-root` fix (SA-0MT1WOWAO000T2P1) and the global fallback used by other framework projects.
- `install_pi.sh` sets `core.hooksPath=.githooks`, so this clone diverges from the documented/reproducible state.

## Suggested resolution
Switch this clone (and any other drifted clones) to `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` so the committed v3 hook runs. Verify end-to-end with `git hook run pre-push` and a simulated `refs/heads/dev` push. Note the v3 pre-push full-suite gate calls `run_tests.py --scope full`, which contends for the host-wide test semaphore.

`wl sync` overwrites a locally-persisted audit result with an older copy, silently reverting a just-written audit (data loss / audit-record corruption).

## Problem

When a `wl sync` runs after a local audit has been persisted (via the canonical audit persister / `wl audit-set`), the locally written audit text is replaced by an older copy of the audit. The item's other fields (status, stage, `needsProducerReview`, comments, description) are preserved, so the store is left internally inconsistent: the lifecycle reflects the new verdict while the stored audit shows a stale verdict.

Observed 2026-09-26 on `LP-0MSPZUD4G007IYGH` in the LLM project (`/home/rgardler/projects/llm`):

1. The audit runner persisted a new `Ready to close: No` audit at `2026-09-26T13:34:32.382Z`; `wl audit-show` read it back immediately (verified).
2. A herdr-scheduled `wl sync` ran (`.worklog/last-sync-time` advanced to `2026-09-26T13:38:00Z`); afterwards `wl audit-show` returned the **old** `2026-08-15T12:59:45.425Z` `Ready to close: Yes` audit.
3. Re-persisted via `persist_audit.py` at `2026-09-26T13:37:27.757Z`; a further `wl sync` reverted it again.
4. Re-persisted once more at `2026-09-26T13:39:21.882Z` (no sync running); it remained stable while no sync ran.

The item's status/stage (`open`/`plan_complete`) and its comments (including ones added after the new audit) survived each sync — only the audit text reverted.

## Evidence

- The synced export `refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data:.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` contains only `workitem` and `comment` records — **no audit field/record at all** (`grep -c '<new-fingerprint>' worklog-data.jsonl` → 0; the `workitem` record keys do not include `audit`).
- Therefore the audit cannot be propagating through the git sync export, yet the old audit reappears after sync — suggesting the audit is not carried by the export and the sync restores/keeps an older audit from another source, or the merge drops local-only audit changes.
- Commands used: `wl audit-show <id> --json`, `persist_audit.py --issue-id <id> --file <report>`, `git for-each-ref refs/worklog/...`, `.worklog/last-sync-time`.
- Worklog prefix: `SA` (this repo). The affected store was `LP` (LLM project).

## Impact

- Audits persisted by the canonical audit runner can be silently reverted, leaving `status`/`stage` inconsistent with the stored audit text (e.g. item demoted to `open`/`plan_complete` while `audit-show` reports a stale `Yes`).
- Operators and orchestrators reading `wl audit-show` can be misled about whether an item is ready to close.
- Concurrent syncs (herdr-scheduled) make the loss deterministic during busy periods, so re-persisting does not reliably fix it.

## Expected behaviour

- A `wl sync` must never downgrade a newer locally-persisted audit to an older one. Merge semantics for audit text should be last-write-wins by audit time (or audits should be excluded from sync-triggered overwrites until pushed).
- If the sync cannot carry audit text in the git export, it must leave the local audit untouched rather than reverting it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Reproduce in a test: persist audit A (older), then a newer audit B on the same item, run the sync/merge path, and assert `wl audit-show` returns B (not A).
2. The synced worklog export either carries audit records/fields, or the sync merge explicitly preserves the newest local audit (documented decision).
3. A sync that cannot represent audits leaves the local audit unchanged (no revert).
4. Regression fixture uses two audits with distinct `auditedAt` timestamps and the real sync export/import path.
5. Existing worklog sync tests pass.

## Notes

- Discovered during the audit of `LP-0MSPZUD4G007IYGH` (proxy usage analysis fast/cheap bucketing). Recording it here as instructed by the operator; out of scope for that audit.
- Related: audit persistence ordering contract (comments before persistence), and the audit freshness gate — a reverted audit text also makes the content-fingerprint freshness gate evaluate against the wrong (older) report.
data.title: wl sync reverts locally-persisted audit results to a stale older audit

## Summary
On a shared host with several agents running implement/test/audit concurrently, the full suite produced environment-induced failures with no code defect:

1. `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py::TestRunTestsGuardFires::*` and
   `tests/test_pytest_path_resolution.py::test_run_tests_spawns_resolved_pytest_when_missing`
   fail with `subprocess.TimeoutExpired ... timed out after 180 seconds`: the nested
   `run_tests.py --scope full` invocation waits for the host-wide "test" semaphore
   (max 2) and exceeds the spawning test's 180 s subprocess timeout.
2. The `live_repo_guard` plugin reports "live-repo mutation detected" at teardown
   when **other agents** push to `origin` (observed `refs/remotes/origin/dev` and
   `refs/heads/wl-*` moving mid-run), even though the suite itself did not mutate
   the checkout.

## Evidence
- SA-0MSN2LIOQ004TON1 validation: an armed full run gave 3249 passed / 0 failures
  with 3 guard teardown errors; another armed run gave 3246 passed / 3 failures
  (two nested-runner 180 s timeouts + one path-resolution timeout); a run with the
  guard stood down passed 3247 with only the guard's own 2 tests failing (expected).
  The failing set changes run-to-run, confirming non-determinism.

## Suggested improvements
- Make the nested-runner tests resilient to test-semaphore saturation (raise/derive
  their subprocess timeout, or inject a test-only slot/`TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`).
- Consider excluding `refs/remotes/origin/*` (and other-actor branch churn) from the
  live-repo guard fingerprint, or only arming it for refs the suite can create.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: Nested `run_tests.py` tests do not time out purely because the host test
  semaphore is busy.
- AC2: The live-repo guard does not fail a run when only external `origin/*` refs move.
- AC3: Full suite is green on a shared host with ≥3 concurrent agent test runs.

## Problem

The audit runner's terminal lifecycle can compute an **invalid** pre-audit status+stage pair and then fail to apply it, leaving the audited work item's lifecycle unresolved.

Observed on `SA-0MSITKWBP007VUJS` during `/skill:audit` (2026-09-27, commit `e365fce2`):

- Captured pre-audit state: `status=blocked`, `stage=in_review`.
- The run ended with an infrastructure-fallback `No` (parent Phase 1 Pi calls stalled — `Local Proxy/plan`, no output for 600 s each), so the restore branch ran with `safe_status=blocked`, `safe_stage=in_review`.
- `wl update --status blocked --stage in_review` was rejected:
  `Invalid status/stage combination: status "blocked" is not compatible with stage "in_review". Allowed stages for status "blocked": idea, intake_complete, plan_complete.`
- After 3 retries, `_restore_pre_audit_state_on_failure` attempted the same invalid pair and also failed:
  `The item's lifecycle is unresolved — check its state with wl show ... and recover manually if needed.`
- `wl doctor` flags the same item as `status-stage.incompatible` with safe fix `status=completed`.

## Root cause

In `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` the restore branch uses `safe_stage = ctx.original_stage` verbatim; the fallback stage is only computed when the stage is empty (`if not safe_stage`). The captured pair is never validated against worklog's `statusStageCompatibility`, so an already-incompatible stored pair is propagated unchanged and rejected by `wl update`.

## Proposed change

Normalise the target pair to a compatible status+stage **before** issuing the `wl update`:

- If `original_stage` is not valid for `original_status`, choose a valid stage (e.g. `plan_complete` for `blocked`, matching the existing empty-stage fallback) or the `wl doctor` safe fix (`status=completed` for stage `in_review`).
- Verify the pair is accepted; surface the normalisation in the diagnostic.
- Apply the same normalisation in `_restore_pre_audit_state_on_failure`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. When the captured pre-audit state is an incompatible status+stage pair (e.g. `blocked`+`in_review`), the terminal restore applies a **valid** pair and verifies it via readback — the item is never left with an unresolved lifecycle.
2. A regression test captures an item whose pre-audit state is an incompatible pair and asserts the terminal lifecycle ends in a valid state (and never retries the known-invalid pair).
3. The runner's diagnostic states the incompatible pair and the normalised pair it applied.
4. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Related work

- discovered-from:SA-0MSITKWBP007VUJS
data.title: Audit runner: invalid pre-audit status+stage pair leaves work item lifecycle unresolved

## Observed

During SA-0MUOO5UEB008RXBP, `implement.py finish` reported `git push to dev failed` and reset the work item to `open` (removing the worktree), but the commit had actually landed on `origin/dev` (origin/dev == dev == 4b25aac4, new file present). `cleanup.terminated: 1` was reported.

## Impact

False failure resets a successfully-implemented item to `open`, risking duplicate work and leaving the item un-in\_review despite the work being on dev. The operator/agent must manually detect and correct the state.

## Likely cause (to confirm)

The push step resolves its timeout from `.pi/test-config.json` `timeoutPerCommand` (1500s) and kills the process group on timeout; the pre-push hook runs the full suite. If the hook/ push exceeds the bound after the remote has accepted the objects, the command is killed and reported as a failure even though the push completed.

## AC

1. `implement.py finish` distinguishes 'push completed' from 'push command interrupted after completion' (e.g. verify the remote ref advanced / commit reachable on origin before reporting failure).
2. On a push that actually landed, the item is advanced to `completed/in_review` (not reset to open) and the commit comment recorded.
3. Regression test covering the push-completed-but-hook-interrupted path.
4. Full suite passes.

# Tune audit queue timeout / concurrency ceiling to eliminate residual bounded-queue saturation

## Problem statement

The bounded priority queue (SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM) eliminated fail-fast audit
re-queueing (27 → 0), but under peak-day traffic **14 items still exhausted the
bounded wait and returned a `bounded-queue saturation` verdict** (latest live
metrics: 3 residual, down from 14 at evaluation time). Per
`docs/dev/downtime-idle-gate-evaluation.md`, this is a **capacity/timeout
problem — not an idle-gate problem**: the configured concurrency ceilings are
lower than the host's real audit-slot capacity, so peak bursts queue beyond
what the timeout bound permits.

## Users

- **Operators** running the herdr downtime dispatcher: they expect audits to
  complete with real verdicts even during peak multi-agent traffic, not return
  an `unmet` "concurrency limit reached" verdict after a full wait.
- **Agent sessions** whose audits time out under saturation: today they burn a
  full bounded wait (90–115 s) and either retry later or leave items stuck in
  `in_review`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Right-sized ceilings:** `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` and/or
   `AUDIT_MAX_HOST_AUDITS` defaults are raised to the host's real audit-slot
   capacity, *measured empirically* via the existing F7 harness
   (`skill/shared/validate_fanout.py` — the largest ceiling that keeps load
   < 16 on the 16-core host with no swap growth), informed by the 3-slot local
   LLM proxy pool.

2. **Timeout stays bash-window-safe:** `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` remains bounded
   (≈90–115 s) inside the parent bash-tool execution window (~120 s), so the
   SA-0MSGEAZMC009LHKL mid-wait-kill failure mode is not reintroduced.

3. **Zero residual saturation:** with N ≥ 3 concurrent audits against a busy
   host, **zero** `bounded-queue saturation` (or `host-wide saturation`)
   `unmet` verdicts are produced — all audits persist **real** verdicts
   (verification mirrors SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM AC1).

4. **No regression:** existing concurrency/queue tests keep passing —
   `test_audit_runner_concurrency.py`, `test_audit_queue_integration.py`,
   `test_audit_slot_lock_contention.py` — including the "timeout ≥ 0.1s < 5s
   bounded wait" behaviour and priority-ordering assertions; no test relies on
   the old default values being treated as constants.

5. **Documentation updated:** `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (fix the
   documented ceiling default — prose currently claims 2 while
   `process_semaphore.py` default is 5), `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`
   (host-cap defaults), and the follow-up status in
   `docs/dev/downtime-idle-gate-evaluation.md`.

6. **Full suite green:** the full project test suite passes with the changes
   (build → test → commit order per AGENTS.md).

## Constraints

- **Do NOT relax the herdr idle gate** (rejected in SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50); no
  ContextHub dispatcher change is in scope.
- Keep priority ordering (critical > high > medium > low; FIFO within tier)
  and the bounded-wait semantics of the shared priority queue unchanged.
- `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` must not exceed the parent bash-tool execution timeout
  (~120 s) unless the dispatch model changes — decoupling the wait from the
  bash-tool window is **out of scope**.
- The host's real capacity is bounded by the local LLM proxy
  (`session_slot_pool_size: 3` default) plus CPU/RAM headroom — the empirical
  F7 measurement is the source of truth.

## Existing state

| Knob | Default | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` | 90.0 s | `audit_runner.py:289-290` | Bounded queue+slot wait; 90s chosen to stay inside bash-tool ~120s window (SA-0MSGEAZMC009LHKL) |
| `AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` | 0.0 s | `audit_runner.py` | Per-attempt fail-fast inside the admission poll; total wait governed by queue timeout |
| `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (`DEFAULT_MAX_WORKERS`) | 5 | `process_semaphore.py:75-76` | `_audit_semaphore_max_workers` precedence: CLI > env > 5 |
| `AUDIT_MAX_HOST_AUDITS` | 3 | `audit_runner.py:250-251` | Host-wide ingress cap (`audit-host` semaphore) |
| `AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` | 90.0 s | `audit_runner.py:252-253` | Bounded wait for host ingress slot |
| Queue `max_depth` | 50 | `queue.py:94` | `QUEUE_MAX_DEPTH` override |

- Latest live metrics (2026-10-13): 771 admissions; bounded-queue saturation
  **3**; host-wide saturation 0; legacy fail-fast 0; max observed wait 599.8 s
  (historical, from a higher-override period).
- No deployment/pi/herdr env overrides for these knobs — **code defaults
  currently govern every project**. The herdr dispatcher sets only
  `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1`.

## Desired change

Raise the audit concurrency ceilings to the **empirically measured** host
capacity (via `validate_fanout.py`, respecting the 3-slot proxy pool), keep
`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` bounded inside the bash-tool window, and update the
defaults + documentation so peak bursts drain through the queue instead of
timing out. Verify with N ≥ 3 concurrent audits against a busy host with zero
concurrency-limit `unmet` verdicts.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — ceiling/timeout defaults
  (`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT`, `AUDIT_MAX_HOST_AUDITS_DEFAULT`,
  `AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT`), `_audit_queue_timeout()`,
  `_acquire_audit_slot()`, `_acquire_host_audit_slot()` (see ~line 3402,
  12468-12554)

relocated-from:AH-0MUVRNAU5005PEUE (AI_Hell worklog), moved to this repo because `implement.py` is agent-infrastructure code owned by SorraAgents (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`).

## Problem

The global implement skill's parent phase (`implement.py parent`) has two gaps that cause epics to loop when a child is externally blocked:

1. **`do-not-delegate` is not honoured.** The herdr dispatcher respects the `do-not-delegate` tag, but `implement.py parent` does not: `_classify_child` returns "implement" for any non-terminal, non-in-progress child and `_next_child_to_implement` selects it regardless of the tag. An epic whose only startable child is guard-tagged will therefore be repeatedly selected and its guarded child re-attempted on every dispatch.

2. **Stale worktree branches are not reused or cleaned.** `git_worktree_add` runs `git worktree add --track -b <branch> <path> <parent>`, which fails if `<branch>` already exists. When a prior `start` aborted after creating the branch but before/at worktree removal, the branch survives and every subsequent `start` fails with a cryptic "Failed to create worktree" error instead of reusing the branch or reporting the stale branch clearly.

Observed on **Switch game audio from procedural Web Audio to ToneForge (AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J)** (session herdr-1791234333-893049-2032): `implement.py parent` selected the externally-blocked, `do-not-delegate` child **Author game-specific ToneForge recipes (AH-0MUTYV8480019Z51)** and then failed worktree creation because the branch `wl-AH-0MUTYV8480019Z51-author-game-specific-toneforge-recipes` already existed.

## Expected behaviour

- `implement.py parent` skips `do-not-delegate` children (reports them as guarded/not startable) unless explicitly overridden.
- `git_worktree_add` either reuses an existing branch that is identical to / fast-forwardable from the parent branch, or fails with an actionable message naming the stale branch and how to recover.
- A failed `start` should not leave a stale branch behind (or should clean it up on abort).

## Scope

- Global implement skill script `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/scripts/implement.py` (`_classify_child`, `_next_child_to_implement`, `git_worktree_add`, `phase_start`/abort path). This is agent-infrastructure code; report/plan changes there, do not edit from an AI_Hell worktree.

## Related

- Complements SA-0MUWNKUIU007N876 (the do-not-delegate-only item relocated from AH-0MUWGZ7UH007NBT4).

# tree_coverage AC extraction ignores numbered Acceptance Criteria lists

Discovered-from: SA-0MUY9PMB7001ENMP (plan session for the implement.py claim bug).

## Problem statement

`skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria` collects only markdown
bullet (`- ` / `+ `) AC entries. Work items whose `## Acceptance Criteria` section uses an
ordered list (`1. `, `2. `, …) yield **zero** extracted ACs. The plan skill's AC coverage
review (`run_coverage_review`) then reports `fully_covered: True` / `coverage_pct: 100`
trivially, so parent→child AC coverage is never actually verified for those items.

Observed on SA-0MUY9PMB7001ENMP, whose `## Acceptance Criteria` section uses a numbered
list: `run_coverage_review` returned `parent_acs: 0`.

## Users

- Agents running `/skill:plan` AC coverage review, who rely on the coverage recommendation
  (`proceed` / `auto_close` / `stop`) to gate `plan_complete`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `extract_acceptance_criteria` recognises ordered-list AC entries (`1. `, `2) `, etc.)
  as well as `- `/`+ ` bullets, preserving entry order and stripping list markers.
- Mixed bullet + numbered sections extract every AC exactly once.
- Unit tests in `skill/shared/tests/` (or the existing test module for `tree_coverage`)
  cover bullet-only, numbered-only and mixed AC sections.
- `run_coverage_review` for an item with numbered ACs returns the real AC count (not 0).

# SorraAgents: decide fate of untracked `skill/pane-triage`

**Headline:** Make the deployed `pane-triage` global skill a tracked, hygiene-compliant member of `SorraAgents/skill` (Option A) instead of leaving it as a locally-excluded untracked copy, so `/skill:pane-triage` is reproducible from a fresh clone and the skill inventory, description-hygiene, and context-budget gates all agree.

## Problem Statement

The SorraAgents main checkout carries a **permanently untracked**
`skill/pane-triage/` directory (locally excluded via `.git/info/exclude`) that is
a deployed copy of the tracked `skill/pane-triage/` in ContextHub. Because
`~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to `SorraAgents/skill`, this copy is what makes
`/skill:pane-triage` available to every pi session, yet it is invisible to a
fresh clone, is excluded from the skill inventory/budget, and (before the
untracked-dir isolation work) failed the hygiene and context-budget gates. A
decision is required: make the skill a first-class tracked global skill in
SorraAgents, or remove the copy.

## Users

- **Producer / operator** — relies on `/skill:pane-triage` to review and close
  idle herdr panes; a removal would silently retire the skill for every
  framework project whose global skills resolve to `SorraAgents/skill`.
  - *As a producer, I want `/skill:pane-triage` to keep working after a fresh
    `git clone` of SorraAgents, so my pane-cleanup workflow is reproducible on
    any machine.*
- **Framework maintainer** — needs the global skill inventory, description
  hygiene, and startup context-budget gate to reflect reality, so an untracked
  directory cannot hide a skill or skew the counts.
  - *As a maintainer, I want every global skill tracked in SorraAgents, so the
    hygiene tests, context-budget thresholds, and install script agree on the
    same skill set.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **The skill is tracked.** `git ls-files skill/pane-triage` in the SorraAgents
   repository lists `SKILL.md`, `__init__.py`, `scripts/pane-triage.py`,
   `scripts/pane_triage.py`, and `tests/test_pane_triage.py`; the
   `skill/pane-triage/` entry is removed from `.git/info/exclude`; a fresh
   checkout of `dev` contains `skill/pane-triage/SKILL.md`.
2. **Doc hygiene passes.** `skill/pane-triage/SKILL.md` passes
   `tests/test_skill_path_conventions.py` (no legacy `skill/<name>/` references
   and no CWD-relative script invocations — commands use
   `$(skill_path pane-triage)/scripts/...`) and
   `tests/test_skill_description_hygiene.py` (frontmatter description ≤140 chars,
   contains "Use when", starts with an action word). `pane-triage` is added to
   `NON_WORK_ITEM_SKILLS` in `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` (it creates or
   updates no work items, so it must not carry the standardized-report final
   step).
3. **Inventory and budget agree.** The expectations in
   `tests/test_skill_description_hygiene.py` are updated for the new tracked
   skill count and total-prose budget (and the reduction-baseline exclusions, if
   applicable); `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` is regenerated with
   `--include-hidden`; `docs/dev/context-budget.md` records a dated bump note
   with justification.
4. **Source parity (no drift).** The ContextHub source `skill/pane-triage/`
   receives the same hygiene edits so the deployed copy and the source do not
   diverge; the tracking/deployment model is documented in
   `docs/pane-triage-skill.md` (ContextHub).
5. **Verification.** The targeted hygiene/context-budget tests
   (`test_skill_description_hygiene.py`, `test_report_wiring_hygiene.py`,
   `test_skill_path_conventions.py`, `test_context_budget_gate.py`,
   `test_pre_push_context_budget_gate.py`) pass with the directory tracked, and
   the context-budget pre-push gate passes on `dev`.
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Repo boundary.** Global skills live in `SorraAgents/skill/` (symlinked to
  `~/.pi/agent/skills` by `SorraAgents/scripts/install_pi.sh`); the `WL-` work
  item is tracked in ContextHub's worklog and its code lands in SorraAgents
  `dev`. This mirrors the machine-hygiene epic (`WL-0MUJLCVRS0093EJJ`).
- **Do not weaken the untracked-dir isolation work.** The filters added by
  `SA-0MUQ96V5W000TMTU` / `SA-0MUU206QT001M66F` / `SA-0MUPDDMXB0088CMM` must
  stay: concurrent agents' genuinely transient `skill/<name>/` WIP must remain
  ignorable. This item removes the *permanent* untracked directory, it does not
  remove the general guard.
- **Runtime dependency is unchanged.** The skill shells out to the ContextHub
  compiled bridge (`packages/herdr/dist/pane-close-cli.js`) via
  `CONTEXTHUB_DIR`/`PANE_TRIAGE_BRIDGE`; committing the Python copy to
  SorraAgents does not move that dependency.
- **No behaviour change** to the skill's classification, approval gate, or
  never-close guards — this is a tracking/hygiene fix only.

## Existing State

- `SorraAgents/skill/pane-triage/` exists and is byte-identical (source files)
  to `ContextHub/skill/pane-triage/`; only `__pycache__/*.pyc` differ.
- The SorraAgents copy is excluded locally by `.git/info/exclude`
  (`skill/pane-triage/`) and is therefore untracked.
- `tests/test_skill_description_hygiene.py` expects exactly 19 tracked skills;
  `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` enumerates the expected skill set from
  `WORK_ITEM_SKILLS + NON_WORK_ITEM_SKILLS + ["report"]`.
- The current 140-char description limit is exceeded by the existing 234-char
  `pane-triage` description, and its `SKILL.md` uses `cd $(skill_path
  pane-triage)` + `./scripts/pane-triage.py` invocations.
- The context-budget gate (`measure_context.py --include-hidden`) currently
  passes because untracked dirs are filtered; committing the directory makes it
  count toward `skills_prose`/`total`.

## Desired Change

Choose **Option A — track the skill in SorraAgents** and make it hygiene-compliant:

1. Move `skill/pane-triage/` from untracked/excluded to tracked in SorraAgents
   `dev`, committing the same files that currently make `/skill:pane-triage`
   work.
2. Sanitise `SKILL.md` for the doc-convention and description-hygiene tests:
   rewrite the frontmatter description to ≤140 chars with a "Use when" clause
   and an action-verb first word; replace the `cd $(skill_path pane-triage); ./scripts/...`
   invocation block with `$(skill_path pane-triage)/scripts/...` forms.
3. Register the skill in `NON_WORK_ITEM_SKILLS`
   (`tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py`) and update the count/total-prose
   expectations (`tests/test_skill_description_hygiene.py`).
4. Regenerate `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` and add a dated bump
   note to `docs/dev/context-budget.md`.
5. Mirror the `SKILL.md` hygiene edits into the ContextHub source copy and
   document the source/deployment relationship in `docs/pane-triage-skill.md`.

The alternative (**Option B — remove the untracked copy**) is rejected: because
SorraAgents is the sole source of the global skills symlink, removing the copy
would silently retire `/skill:pane-triage` for every framework project while the
skill remains documented and referenced as deployed. Retiring the skill is a
materially larger product decision that should be raised separately if desired.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/pane-triage/SKILL.md` — rewrite description (≤140 chars, "Use when") and script-invocation forms.
- `skill/pane-triage/__init__.py`, `skill/pane-triage/scripts/pane-triage.py`, `skill/pane-triage/scripts/pane_triage.py`, `skill/pane-triage/tests/test_pane_triage.py` — new tracked files (SorraAgents).
- `tests/test_skill_description_hygiene.py` — update expected skill count and total-prose budget.
- `tests/test_report_wiring_hygiene.py` — add `pane-triage` to `NON_WORK_ITEM_SKILLS`.
- `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` — regenerate with `--include-hidden`.
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` — dated threshold bump note.
- `.git/info/exclude` — remove the `skill/pane-triage/` entry (local, untracked).
- `ContextHub/skill/pane-triage/SKILL.md` — mirror the hygiene edits (source parity).
- `ContextHub/docs/pane-triage-skill.md` — document the tracking/deployment model.

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk (highest):** committing the skill pulls in a mandatory
  `SKILL.md` rewrite, two hygiene-list/test updates, and a context-budget
  threshold regeneration. Extra opportunities (e.g. retiring the ContextHub
  duplicate, generalising untracked-dir sync) must be recorded as linked work
  items, not absorbed here.
- **Drift risk:** editing only the SorraAgents copy leaves the ContextHub source
  divergent; AC4 mandates mirroring the edits and documenting the relationship.
- **Gate-weakening risk:** the fix must not delete the untracked-dir isolation
  filters; a genuinely transient WIP directory must stay ignorable.
- **Regression risk:** the skill's runtime bridge lives in ContextHub; the
  commit must not alter the `CONTEXTHUB_DIR`/`PANE_TRIAGE_BRIDGE` resolution or
  the approval gate.
- **Assumption:** the deployed copy is the intended artifact (not accidental) —
  supported by `docs/pane-triage-skill.md` and the active global registration.
- **Assumption:** ContextHub remains the source-of-truth repo for the skill and
  the deployed SorraAgents copy is a mirror.

## Related Work

- `WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM` — Create pane-triage skill (the skill itself; records the
  "skills are Python-only (`SorraAgents/skill/`)" placement decision).
- `WL-0MUJLCVRS0093EJJ` — machine-hygiene epic; surfaced this untracked copy and
  established the global-skill → SorraAgents commit precedent.
- `SA-0MUQ96V5W000TMTU` / `SA-0MUU206QT001M66F` / `SA-0MUPDDMXB0088CMM` —
  untracked-skill-dir isolation (the guard that must not be weakened).
- `WL-0MUJW9EEP009Q0V3` — shared classifier + automatic reaper (runtime
  dependency of the skill).
- `WL-0MUJW9FY5008KBTQ` — coordinate pane-triage reuse and document closure.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (agent, evidence-based determination):** Commit the untracked
  `skill/pane-triage` to SorraAgents, or remove it? — **Answer (agent, derived
  from repo evidence):** Commit (Option A). Evidence:
  `ContextHub/docs/pane-triage-skill.md` states the skill is "tracked in
  ContextHub; deployed to the global skills directory as `/skill:pane-triage`";
  `SorraAgents/scripts/install_pi.sh` symlinks `~/.pi/agent/skills` →
  `SorraAgents/skill`, so SorraAgents is the only source of global skills; the
  producer recorded that "skills are Python-only (`SorraAgents/skill/`)" in
  `WL-0MUJMXVPO0016DZM`; and `WL-0MUJLCVRS0093EJJ` established the precedent that
  global skills must be committed in SorraAgents. Removing the copy would break
  `/skill:pane-triage` globally. Source: repo inspection + worklog evidence.
- **OPEN QUESTION (producer confirmation):** Option A is a design decision for a
  tracked global skill, not merely a cleanup. Please confirm during review, or
  raise Option B (retire `/skill:pane-triage`) as a separate work item. Context:
  no producer response was available in this intake session.
- **Q (scope):** Should the redundant ContextHub `skill/pane-triage/` copy be
  removed? — **Answer (assumed):** No — keep ContextHub as the documented
  source-of-truth and mirror the hygiene edits (AC4); removing it would change
  ContextHub's context-budget surface and tests and is out of scope. Recorded as
  an assumption.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MSM3STQ0008QUMG** – [test-failure] should have no legacy skill/ path references (Skill: cleanup) — failing test (completed)
- **WL-0MR24H2VK004PAQ7** – 1a: Error Classification & Settings (tests) (completed)

- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: agent, budget, byte, checkout, commit (+36 more)

# Prefer interface/behaviour assertions over toHaveBeenCalledWith on internal collaborators

## Goal

As a test-suite maintainer, I want guidance and enforcement that discourage asserting on calls to internal collaborators with `toHaveBeenCalledWith`, so tests verify observable behaviour rather than implementation wiring.

## Background

The ContextHub test-churn analysis (WL-0MUZRNLFT004H8XJ) found the largest test file, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` (13,103 lines, 837 tests, 679 `vi.fn()` calls), asserts heavily on internal collaborators, e.g. `expect(resolveProjectWorkspace).toHaveBeenCalledWith('/repo')`. High mock density coupled to call-argument assertions makes suites fragile under refactoring and inflates maintenance cost without improving defect detection.

The repo already curates `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` with related anti-patterns; this work extends it rather than creating a new document.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` gains a new anti-pattern entry: call-argument assertions on internal collaborators (`toHaveBeenCalledWith`, `toHaveBeenNthCalledWith`) with a clear rationale and a positive alternative.
2. The entry distinguishes legitimate cases (asserting an external boundary, e.g. a network or filesystem call, or that a side effect occurred) from the anti-pattern (pinning a private collaborator's exact arguments).
3. At least one concrete before/after example from the codebase is included.
4. `skill/test/SKILL.md` (or the relevant review workflow) references the guidance so reviewers apply it.
5. Tests or lint cover any automated detection added, and the suite passes.

## Related work

- ContextHub WL-0MUZRNLFT004H8XJ (evidencing analysis)
- ContextHub WL-0MSG7ZTC000163FL (downtime-worker test suite, source of the example)

# Add a tests-deleted-vs-added health metric and actively prune tests that no longer map to behaviour

## Problem statement

The test-churn analysis currently reports test *additions* and *rewrites* but makes test *deletions* nearly invisible: whole-file deletions are hidden by the default diff filter, and there is no consolidated "tests added vs tests deleted vs net growth" figure per project or per test area. As a result the suite grows roughly 8:1 (82,381 added vs 9,968 deleted lines in modified test files, from the ContextHub analysis) with no health signal and no documented way to prune tests that no longer map to observable behaviour.

## Users

- **Maintainer of the pi agent infrastructure** — wants an honest, consolidated growth metric (added / deleted / modified / net growth) per project and per test area, in both the human report and JSON, so suite growth is visible at a glance without additional analysis.
- **Producer / engineering manager** — wants a trended growth signal over time (per calendar quarter) so regressions in net test growth are visible.
- **Agent enforcing testing policy** — wants a documented, repeatable workflow to identify and remove tests that no longer map to observable behaviour, referencing `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`.

Example user stories:

- As a maintainer, I want the report to state, per project and per test area, exactly how many tests were added, deleted, modified, and the net growth, so I can see at a glance whether the suite is growing without bound.
- As a producer, I want the added/deleted/net-growth metric trended per calendar quarter, so regressions in test-suite growth are visible over time.
- As an agent, I want a documented review workflow for pruning tests that no longer map to observable behaviour, so pruning decisions rest on the metric plus explicit criteria rather than anecdote.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The analysis reports, per project and per test area: tests added, tests deleted, tests modified, and net growth, in the human report and JSON.
2. Whole-file test deletions are counted (diff filter includes `D`; rename detection applied so moves are not miscounted as deletions).
3. A documented review workflow describes how to identify and remove tests that no longer map to observable behaviour, referencing `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`.
4. The growth metric is trended over time **per calendar quarter** (derived from commit dates), so regressions are visible.
5. Tests cover the added/deleted accounting, including files deleted and re-added.
6. The metric is exposed by the reproducible `skill/test-churn` skill rather than as a standalone script.
7. At least one testing/validation criterion: the full project test suite passes with the new changes.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the skill README/SKILL.md, and `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md`.

## Constraints

- Must live inside the existing `skill/test-churn` skill (AC6); no new standalone script and no ContextHub-specific paths.
- The metric must be derived deterministically from git history via the existing analyser entry point (`skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py`), which is read-only against the analysed repository.
- Changes must not regress the corrected methodology implemented under `SA-0MV2JE6MG003B0SW` (real git name-status, documented rewrite-ratio denominators, distinct-commit temporal rates, whole-file deletion accounting).
- Growth trend granularity is calendar quarter derived from commit dates (operator decision Q2); release/tag-based grouping is out of scope.
- The item delivers metric + documented workflow only; the actual pruning pass is a follow-on item, not part of this work (operator decision Q3).
- Work item descriptions/comments in Markdown, UK English.

## Existing state

- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py` already computes: `modified_test_deletions`, `modified_test_additions`, `new_test_file_additions`, `deleted_test_files`, `deleted_test_lines`, and per-area `new_files` / `deleted_files` / `total_added` / `total_deleted` / `rewrites`.
- Whole-file deletion accounting exists (spans whole history, including test-only commits) and `--diff-filter=ADMRT` already includes `D`; AC2 is *mostly* satisfied but lacks explicit tests for delete-and-re-add.
- The temporal trend (`analyse_temporal_trends`) is currently **monthly rewrite-rate** only — there is no quarterly net-growth trend (AC4 is new work).
- No consolidated net-growth figure and no documented pruning workflow exist (AC1 headline and AC3 are new work).
- The skill's tests (`skill/test-churn/tests/`) cover deletion accounting in test-only commits and rename detection, but not file deleted and re-added (AC5 gap).

## Desired change

1. Add per-project and per-area accounting: **tests added, tests deleted, tests modified, net growth** (files and/or lines, consistently defined and documented) in `test_churn_data.json` and the human report.
2. Add a **quarterly net-growth trend** (per calendar quarter derived from commit dates) alongside or extending the existing temporal trend, in report and JSON.
3. Add a **documented review workflow** for pruning tests that no longer map to observable behaviour, referencing `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` (in the skill SKILL.md and/or the dev reference doc).
4. Add tests covering added/deleted accounting including files deleted and re-added; update the skill reference documentation.

## Key Files

- `skill/test-churn/scripts/test_churn_analysis.py` — add consolidated net-growth metric, quarterly growth trend, human-report + JSON sections.
- `skill/test-churn/SKILL.md` — document the new metric and the pruning review workflow (referencing `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`).
- `skill/test-churn/tests/test_test_churn_analysis.py` — tests for added/deleted accounting including delete-and-re-add.
- `docs/dev/test-churn-skill-reference.md` — metric definitions, methodology and worked examples updated.

## Risks, assumptions & scope control

- **Assumption:** "net growth" is defined as additions minus deletions per project/area (files and lines reported separately), with the definitions documented so figures are unambiguous.
- **Assumption:** quarterly grouping is derived from commit dates on the analysed mainline; an empty quarter is reported as zero rather than omitted.
- **Risk:** renames are miscounted as delete+add if rename detection is misconfigured — mitigated by keeping `--diff-filter=ADMRT` + rename detection and covering moves in tests (existing `test_parse_name_status_handles_renames_and_plain_statuses`).
- **Risk:** the consolidated metric duplicates or contradicts existing fields, causing report confusion — mitigated by documenting the mapping from new fields to current ones in the reference doc.
- **Failure mode:** a file deleted and re-added in the same history could be under- or double-counted — covered explicitly by a new test (AC5).
- **Scope creep:** actually pruning dead tests from a suite is a distinct, higher-risk change; it is tracked as a follow-on work item (operator decision Q3), not part of this item.

## Related work

- Epic parent: `SA-0MV28WNFY009DF6Y` *Migrate test-churn / TDD-value analysis to SorraAgents and make reporting reproducible* (completed; recorded dependency).
- `SA-0MV2JE6MG003B0SW` *Fix test churn analysis status detection and rewrite-ratio denominator* (completed; methodology this work must not regress).
- `SA-0MV28WS5G004YNNS` *Create the reproducible test-churn reporting skill* (completed; the skill this metric extends).
- `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` — referenced by the pruning workflow (AC3).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What does 'per project' mean in AC1?" — Answer (operator, interactive reply): "A: the single analysed project's own report headings (project total + per-area breakdown)". Source: interactive reply in intake session. Research: existing analyser is single-project-root; multi-repo batch/aggregation is out of scope (potentially covered by `SA-0MV28WYLU001BMFU` scheduled runs).
- Q2: "AC4 says 'per quarter or per release' — which granularity should the growth trend use?" — Answer (operator): "a: calendar quarter, derived from commit dates". Source: interactive reply. Research: quarters are universally derivable and deterministic; tag-based/release grouping is out of scope.
- Q3: "AC3 + title say 'actively prune'. Should this item actually remove dead tests now, or deliver metric + documented workflow with pruning as a follow-on?" — Answer (operator): "a: deliver metric + documented review workflow only; pruning is a follow-on item". Source: interactive reply. Research: removing suite tests is a distinct, higher-risk change needing its own evidence and review; it will be tracked separately as a follow-on work item.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MUIYHI12000XVM0** – Migrate remaining raw-git test helpers to skill/shared/git_sandbox (open)
- **SA-0MS31SAM20004GTJ** – all actions should leave the status in a good state (completed)
- **SA-0MSHZ08OE0033049** – Remove AMPA documentation (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: acceptance, actively, add, added, also (+72 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: acceptance, add, also, analysis, applied (+66 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: acceptance, actively, add, added, also (+60 more)

# Run mutation testing on top-churn modules to measure real test value

## Goal

As a producer, I want an empirical measure of whether the largest test suites actually detect faults, so conclusions about TDD return on investment rest on evidence rather than churn proxies.

## Background

Churn and line-count metrics cannot tell us whether tests earn their keep. The top-churn / largest suites identified by the ContextHub analysis (e.g. `downtime-worker.test.ts`, `worklist.test.ts`, `coordination-dispatch.test.ts`, `sync.test.ts`, `database.test.ts`) are mock-heavy; mutation testing directly measures whether they detect injected faults. This is the recommended follow-up before firm TDD-ROI conclusions in WL-0MUZRNLFT004H8XJ.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A mutation-testing tool is selected and documented (e.g. Stryker for TypeScript, mutmut for Python), with rationale and licensing.
2. The tool runs against at least the top three churn modules of a target project and reports a mutation score per module and overall.
3. Results are compared with test size/mock density to test the hypothesis that high-volume mock-heavy suites have lower mutation scores.
4. Findings are written up and appended to the TDD-value assessment, with explicit caveats (sampling, runtime cost, equivalent mutants).
5. The campaign is reproducible (pinned tool version, documented command) and does not regress the project test suite.
6. Runtime cost is measured and bounded so the campaign can be run periodically.

## Depends on

The reproducible test-churn skill migration epic (provides top-churn input).

# Create scheduled tasks to run the test-churn skill on all projects

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want the test-churn / test-health skill to run automatically on a schedule across all local projects, so test-suite growth and rewrite trends are monitored continuously without manual effort.

## Background

SorraAgents already supports scheduled prompts via `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` (entries with `id`, `prompt`, `intervalDays`, optional `time`, `lastTriggeredAt`), used by e.g. `/skill:refactor` and `/skill:standup`. The new test-churn skill should be registered the same way for each project.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A scheduled entry is added for the test-churn/test-health skill in `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` (or the project-appropriate scheduled-prompts file) using the existing schema.
2. The schedule runs for every managed project, either via per-project entries or a single command that iterates configured project roots.
3. Output is written to a predictable location (e.g. `reports/test-churn/<date>.md`) and is idempotent (a re-run does not create duplicates).
4. Failures are surfaced (non-zero exit / logged) and do not silently pass.
5. The schedule interval is configurable and documented; the default is documented with a rationale.
6. Tests cover the scheduled-entry wiring or the iteration/adapter used to fan out across projects.
7. The setup is documented in the skill's SKILL.md and in the SorraAgents README/docs.

## Depends on

The reproducible test-churn skill migration epic (the skill must exist first).

## Problem statement

The test skill's runner (`test/scripts/run_tests.py`) reports a **false PASS** when invoked with the name-based ``--suite node`` flag on a repo whose real suite is vitest driven through an npm ``test`` script. The resolver returns an empty command list, executes nothing, exits 0, and (in the caching paths) records a green entry — so callers believe the Node/vitest suite ran when it did not.

This was found while investigating the AI_Hell repo (an npm/vitest project with co-located `src/**/*.test.ts` and no `tests/{node,cli,unit}` directories).

## Reproduction

From an npm/vitest repo (AI_Hell):

```bash
python3 ~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py --suite node --force --json
```

Result:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "suites": {
    "node": {
      "success": true,
      "returncode": 0,
      "command": "",
      "failures": [],
      "cached": false,
      "scope": "full"
    }
  }
}
```

The real suite for the same repo resolves correctly only via the default `all` suite:

```bash
python3 ~/.pi/agent/skills/test/scripts/run_tests.py --suite all --force --json   # command: "npm --silent test"
```

## Root cause

In `run_suite()` (default test type), name-based resolution is:

- `name == "pytest"` → `[pytest_command()]`
- `name == "node"` → `node_suite_commands(cwd)`
- `name == "all"` → `full_suite_commands(cwd)`

`node_suite_commands()` only emits commands for existing `tests/{node,cli,unit}` directories and never consults the `.pi/test-config.json` extension file nor the npm-test convention. `full_suite_commands()` is the documented single source of truth and resolves extension `suiteCommands` → pytest → node dirs → **npm-test convention**; the `node` name path bypasses all of that.

Related coupling: `filter_commands_for_suite("node", …)` only keeps commands containing the substring `"node"`, so a declared `suiteCommands: ["npx vitest run"]` is also filtered out on the type-profile path.

## Impact

- Any explicit `--suite node` run on such a repo is a silent no-op reported as green (false verification evidence).
- `run_summary --suite node` reports a cache miss even after the full suite has run.
- Lower impact than the `all` path because the default `--suite all` and the audit/implement consumers use `full_suite_commands` and are correct; no known in-repo consumer invokes `--suite node`.

## Expected behaviour

A request for the `node` suite on a repo that has a Node/vitest suite must execute that suite (never an empty command set). Concretely, name-based `node` resolution should fall back in the same order as `full_suite_commands` when `node_suite_commands()` yields nothing, and `filter_commands_for_suite("node", …)` should treat declared non-`node`-substring commands (e.g. `npx vitest run`) as Node-suite commands, or the resolution order should be centralised so all suite names share one convention path.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `--suite node` on an npm/vitest repo with no `tests/{node,cli,unit}` dirs resolves the same command as the npm-test convention (`npm --silent test`) or the declared `suiteCommands` (e.g. `npx vitest run`), and executes it.
2. An empty resolved command set is never reported as `success: true` for an explicitly requested suite that the repo can support; it either runs the fallback or fails with a clear diagnostic.
3. Regression tests cover: node-suite fallback to the npm-test convention; node-suite fallback to declared `suiteCommands`; `filter_commands_for_suite("node", ["npx vitest run"])` behaviour.
4. Existing full-suite / audit / implement cache-key contracts are unchanged (the `all` path behaviour is preserved).
5. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Evidence / references

- Originating work item: `AH-0MV53ABBU008FKE0` (AI_Hell worklog).
- Test skill: `test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `run_suite()`, `node_suite_commands()`, `full_suite_commands()`, `filter_commands_for_suite()`.
- Documented resolution order: `test/SKILL.md` § "Suite-command resolution order (F2)".
- Related: `SA-0MSF8KNE3003JDVD` (node --test directory invocation), `SA-0MSJELL44009XYIL` (skip missing suite dirs).

# Ship post-release branch cleanup fails non-deterministically (shared /tmp report path / concurrent agents)

## Problem statement

The ship skill's post-release branch cleanup (`runPostReleaseCleanup` in
`skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`) fails non-deterministically in a
multi-agent (herdr) environment because it reads and writes a **fixed shared
temp path** (`${os.tmpdir()}/cleanup-summary.json`): when two release/cleanup
processes run concurrently, one clobbers the other's report, so the run logs
"Failed to read summarize report; skipping local cleanup.", then silently
reports "Found 0 merged local branch(es)" and "Pruned 0 local branch(es)" as
if the repository were clean, and the follow-on remote prune also fails.
Observed during the AI_Hell v0.1.10 dev→main release; the same scripts succeed
when re-run standalone.

## Users

- **Agents (Map / herdr):** run automated releases and must not be misled by a
  false "clean" cleanup results.
- **Operators:** trust that post-release cleanup either happened or produced an
  actionable, non-silent warning.
- **Other projects consuming the shared ship/cleanup skills** (AI_Hell, etc.):
  any project can hit the race when releases coincide.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Post-release cleanup uses a **unique temp path per run** (e.g. derived from
   `mkdtempSync`) for the summarize report; a unit test with two
   concurrent-invocation fakes proves no shared-path clobber.
2. A failed `summarize_branches.py` run or report read no longer silently
   reports "0 merged branches" as if the repo were clean — it logs a distinct,
   actionable warning naming the deterministic remediation (unique temp path).
3. The cleanup stays **non-blocking**: a cleanup failure never changes the
   release exit code (existing AC3 preserved).
4. A transient failure (summarize run / report read / remote prune) is
   **retried once** before the actionable warning is emitted.

## Constraints

- Fix must live in the **SorraAgents** repo (ship/cleanup skills are symlinked
  from `~/.pi/agent/skills` into `SorraAgents/skill/`); AI_Hell does not vendor
  these files.
- Cleanup scripts' standalone behaviour (`summarize_branches.py`,
  `prune_local_branches.py`, `delete_remote_branches.py`) must not change.
- Non-blocking guarantee must be preserved (existing AC3 of
  SA-0MUV2W2P7004HVIG).
- Tests run under `node --test "tests/unit/**/*.mjs"` in SorraAgents.

## Existing state

`runPostReleaseCleanup` passes a fixed `${tempDir}/cleanup-summary.json` to
`summarize_branches.py --report` (~L1110) and reads it back (~L1135). On read
failure it sets `reportData = { branches: [] }` and logs only the generic
"skipping local cleanup" warning, then proceeds to report "Found 0 merged local
branch(es)". The branches-to-delete file already uses `mkdtempSync`
(`cleanup-branches-*`), so only the report path is shared.

## Desired change

- Derive a unique report path per run (mkdtemp-based) used for both the
  `--report` argument and the read-back, so concurrent runs cannot clobber.
- Distinguish a real "no merged branches" result from a failed enumerate/read:
  log an actionable warning (unique-path remediation) instead of the misleading
  "0 merged branches".
- Add a single retry with small backoff for the transient step(s) before
  emitting the warning, preserving non-blocking behaviour.
- Extend `tests/unit/test-run-release-cleanup.mjs` with the concurrency-clobber
  test and report-failure-warning test.

## Key Files:

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — `runPostReleaseCleanup` (report path
  L1110/L1135, retry logic, warning text)
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-cleanup.mjs` — new AC1 concurrency fake test,
  AC2 warning test, AC4 retry test

## Risks & assumptions

- **Retry must not mask real errors** — the single retry is for transient
  failures only; the actionable warning must still be emitted on the second
  failure (assumption: failures are quiet enough to retry once without
  doubling wall-clock time; mitigation: small backoff).
- **Scope creep** — deeper cleanup-skill refactoring, branch-deletion policy
  changes, or fixing `delete_remote_branches.py`/`summarize_branches.py`
  behaviour are out of scope; if such work is discovered, record it as new
  linked work items (not here).
- **Test isolation** — the concurrency test must not touch the real
  `/tmp/cleanup-summary.json` or run real git commands; fakes only
  (assumption: existing `setupRunReleaseFixture` harness is reused/adapted).
- **Cross-repo tracking** — item originated in the AI_Hell worklog
  (AH-0MUZGWL14001E1EU, moved here per producer decision Q1c); AI_Hell leaves
  no orphan reference after deletion.
- **Non-blocking guarantee** — AC3 must survive the retry addition; the retry
  must also be non-blocking.

## Related work

- SA-0MUV2W2P7004HVIG — Automate post-release cleanup (introduced this code).
- AH-0MTXLWCWO005OSCZ — Discord notification fails (precedent: ship-skill bug
  tracked in AH worklog, fixed in SorraAgents).
- SA-0MUII5QDI005U2AH — Live-repo guard concurrency (related concurrency issue).
- SA-0MUJQ5BPF001PICU — Test-suite flakiness under concurrent agent load.
- discovered-from: AH-0MUZGWL14001E1EU (moved from AI_Hell worklog);
  discovered-from: release-v0.1.10.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where should the fix be implemented/tracked? The code lives in
  SorraAgents (ship/cleanup skills); this item is tracked in the AI_Hell
  worklog." — Answer (producer): **(c)** "check an equivalent doesn't already
  exist first, delete this item" (i.e. move the item entirely to SorraAgents).
  Source: interactive reply. Research: searched the SorraAgents worklog for
  `cleanup-summary`, `runPostReleaseCleanup`, `post-release cleanup`, `tmp
  path`, `shared report`, `concurrent agents`, `branch cleanup` — no equivalent
  open/closed item; only the completed feature SA-0MUV2W2P7004HVIG and two
  unrelated concurrency items. Outcome: created SA-0MV6JQP9K004QGUT here and
  deleted AH-0MUZGWL14001E1EU.
- Q2: "Is 'retry once' in scope? Expected Behaviour promises it but the ACs do
  not require it." — Answer (producer): **(a)** add it as AC4. Source:
  interactive reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MS3ATINN006QT1M** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/cleanup/scripts/inspect_current_branch.py:28 — Do not catch blind exception: `Exception` (BLE001) (completed)
- **SA-0MS3ATJR7003CK2B** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/cleanup/scripts/prune_local_branches.py:38 — Do not catch blind exception: `Exception` (BLE001) (completed)
- **SA-0MSMT0B3E009NTB7** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_cleanup_scripts.py:1 — Import block is un-sorted or un-formatted (I001) (open)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+162 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+154 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance, actionable (+144 more)

- [ ]  reads session logs from , sorted by file modification time, limited to the 20 most recent.

## Problem Statement

Once session logs are parsed, the skill must extract repeated confusion patterns using deterministic heuristics — tool call distribution, thinking-content error signals, tool result errors, and retry/self-correction patterns. Raw logs are too large and noisy to send to an LLM directly.

## Goal

As a skill author, I want deterministic heuristic extraction of confusion signals from parsed sessions — counts, distributions, and capped excerpts — so the LLM classification stage receives compact, distilled input.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Tool call distribution: counts of each tool name across the 20 sessions, with per-tool error rates.
- [ ] Thinking-content error signals: detect keywords (`error`, `fail`, `retry`, `incorrect`, `sorry`, `wrong`, `fix`, `correct`, `issue`, `problem`, `confused`, `wait`, `actually`, `oh`, `hmm`, `ah`) in thinking content, with a context window around each hit.
- [ ] Tool result errors: detect tracebacks, `permission denied`, `command not found`, and shell expansion errors in `toolResult` content where `isError == true` or content text matches error patterns.
- [ ] Retry/self-correction patterns: detect repeated tool calls with identical arguments within a session, and detect sequences of (tool call → error result → modified tool call).
- [ ] False-positive mitigation: keyword matches are context-windowed; known legitimate uses (e.g. "error handling" in code text) are classified with surrounding context so the LLM can confirm.
- [ ] Per-session excerpt size is capped (configurable, default e.g. 2 KB/session) to bound the LLM prompt.
- [ ] Unit tests cover each signal type with synthetic session fixtures, including at least one borderline false-positive case.
- [ ] A `--max-sessions` and `--errors-only` CLI flag are exposed (or documented as function arguments) for deterministic testing.

## Constraints

- Deterministic and side-effect free: no LLM calls, no file writes.
- Configurable keyword lists (module-level constants) so tests and future tuning are easy.
- Excerpts must never exceed the configured cap.

## Key Files

- `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/agent_log_review.py` — heuristic extraction functions (`extract_tool_distribution`, `extract_thinking_signals`, `extract_tool_errors`, `extract_retry_patterns`)
- `skill/agent-log-review/tests/test_agent_log_review.py` — heuristic unit tests

## Dependencies

- Feature 1 (session log parser) — must be complete first.

## Problem Statement

Heuristic signals are useful but noisy. The skill needs LLM-assisted interpretation to classify patterns into categories (e.g. "skill invocation confusion", "shell quoting issues", "Python import omissions", "permission issues") and generate actionable recommendations — without sending raw multi-megabyte logs to the model.

## Goal

As a skill author, I want an LLM classification stage that sends only distilled heuristic signals (counts + capped excerpts) to a non-interactive `pi` call and receives structured pattern categories plus recommendations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Invokes `pi -p --print` (non-interactive mode) following the audit skill's `_call_pi()` pattern for subprocess LLM calls.
- [ ] Prompt contains only distilled signals (counts, distributions, capped excerpts) — never raw session log content.
- [ ] Requested output is structured JSON (via prompt instruction) with fields: `categories` (list of `{name, confidence, evidence_sessions, summary}`) and `recommendations` (list of `{title, issue_type, target_skill, rationale, evidence_sessions}`).
- [ ] Response parsing is fail-soft: malformed JSON from the model degrades to a diagnostic error rather than a crash.
- [ ] Session IDs of the analysed sessions are included in the prompt so evidence citations map back.
- [ ] Integration test uses a mocked `pi` subprocess (injected via a callable or subprocess runner) to assert: (a) the prompt excludes raw log content, (b) prompt size stays under a documented budget (e.g. 32 KB), (c) a well-formed model response parses into categories and recommendations, (d) a malformed response is handled without raising.
- [ ] No secrets are sent: heuristic excerpts pass through the same redaction used by the report (see Feature 4).

## Constraints

- Hybrid approach: heuristics do extraction, LLM does classification — never LLM-only.
- Single LLM call per run (cost control): all signals batched into one prompt.
- Whisper: no tools enabled for the classification call (`--no-tools` or equivalent) so the model returns text only; follow the audit skill's context-reduction flags where applicable.
- Model selection configurable (default to the project's local proxy model), with a `--model` flag.

## Key Files

- `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/agent_log_review.py` — `classify_patterns(signals, model=..., runner=...)` function and `_call_pi(prompt, model)` helper
- `skill/agent-log-review/tests/test_agent_log_review.py` — mocked-pi classification tests

## Dependencies

- Feature 2 (heuristic pattern extraction) — must be complete first.

## Problem Statement

The skill must present its findings as a structured report in the agent response — summary of findings, top patterns by frequency, recommended skill improvements, and evidence citations — in a deterministic, machine-readable form.

## Goal

As an operator, I want a deterministic report rendered to stdout (Markdown) with an optional `--json` mode for machine consumption, so I can review and cite the analysis.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Report has a clear summary section: number of sessions analysed, date range, sessions skipped (fail-soft counters).
- [ ] Top patterns section: sorted by frequency (descending) then alphabetically (deterministic ordering), each with count and evidence session citations.
- [ ] Recommended improvements section: each recommendation with rationale and evidence citations listing which sessions showed which pattern.
- [ ] Evidence citations use session file names, not full paths, and reference specific pattern occurrences (e.g. "sessions: a.jsonl, b.jsonl").
- [ ] `--json` flag emits the full report as a single JSON document (structured, machine-readable).
- [ ] Human-readable (default) mode emits Markdown with all required sections.
- [ ] Output is deterministic for the same input directory: sorting is explicit everywhere.
- [ ] Secrets redaction is applied to all output (paths matching `.ssh`/`.env`, API key patterns like `sk-...`, `Bearer ...`) before rendering.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: (a) report rendering with required sections, (b) deterministic ordering, (c) `--json` structure, (d) redaction of secret-like strings.

## Constraints

- Print to stdout by default; support optional `--output-file` for the Markdown report (written to `.worklog/tmp/`).
- No side effects on the worklog — reporting is read-only.

## Key Files

- `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/agent_log_review.py` — `render_report(analysis, fmt=...)`, `redact_secrets(text)` functions
- `skill/agent-log-review/tests/test_agent_log_review.py` — report and redaction tests

## Dependencies

- Feature 3 (LLM classification) — must be complete first.

## Problem Statement

Per the parent work item's acceptance criteria, actionable recommendations must be filed as worklog comments on the parent item, and each recommendation must auto-create a child work item (issue-type `chore` or `feature`, assigned to Map, linked via `related-to:<parent-id>` in the description). This is the automation that closes the loop between analysis and skill improvement.

## Goal

As an operator, I want the skill to file recommendations as worklog comments and auto-create child work items (without implementing them), so improvement suggestions are tracked and prioritised downstream.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After a successful analysis, the skill files the report's recommendations as a worklog comment on the parent work item (the item from which the skill was invoked, i.e. CWD project's parent if determinable else an explicit `--parent-id` argument).
- [ ] For each recommendation, a child work item is auto-created with issue-type `chore` or `feature` (chosen per recommendation), priority `low` or `medium`, assigned to `Map`.
- [ ] Each created child's description links back via `related-to:<parent-id>` so traceability is bidirectional.
- [ ] Idempotence: re-running the skill on the same recommendations does not create duplicate child items — same-title items are reused (matched by title), and a reference to the existing item is recorded instead.
- [ ] The parent work item's ACs do NOT get implemented here — work-item creation only, no code changes.
- [ ] A dry-run flag (`--dry-run`) prints what would be created without mutating the worklog.
- [ ] Unit tests (mocked `wl` runner) cover: (a) comment filing, (b) child creation with correct issue-type/assignee/linking, (c) idempotent re-run, (d) dry-run performs no mutations.

## Constraints

- Use `wl` commands via the worklog-safe runner (worktree-aware) exactly as the rest of the tooling does.
- Creation is conservative: only recommendations with LLM-confirmed high confidence are auto-created (configurable threshold).
- No auto-fix/auto-edit of skills — creation only (scope guard from parent intake).

## Key Files

- `skill/agent-log-review/scripts/agent_log_review.py` — `file_recommendations(recs, wl_runner=..., ..., dry_run=False)` functions
- `skill/agent-log-review/tests/test_agent_log_review.py` — mocked-wl integration tests

## Dependencies

- Feature 4 (report rendering) — must be complete first.

# Ship skill: release flow leaves derived version files stale — regenerate post-bump

## Headline

The ship skill's release flow bumps `package.json` but never regenerates consumer
repos' auto-generated version files (e.g. ContextHub `src/version.ts`), so a
release can ship with a stale derived version until the next build runs —
breaking version-parity tests. Fix: the release flow runs the repo's `npm run build`
after the bump (non-fatally) and commits the regenerated tracked files.

## Problem statement

The ship release flow (`merge-dev-to-main.sh` → `bump-version.js`) increments the
version in **`package.json` only**. Consumer repositories that derive a
CLI/runtime version from `package.json` via a build step (e.g. ContextHub's
auto-generated `src/version.ts`, written by `scripts/generate-version.cjs` during
`npm run build`) are left with a **stale derived version** until the next build
runs, so version-parity assertions fail right after a release.

## Users

- **Consumer repo maintainers** (e.g. ContextHub) whose repo derives a CLI/runtime
  version from `package.json` and tracks the derived file (and whose tests assert
  version parity).
  - *User story:* "As a maintainer of a consumer CLI repo, I want the ship release
    to regenerate my derived version file so that my version-parity tests are green
    immediately after a release, without me manually running `npm run build`."
- **Release operators** running `/skill:ship release` — want the release to never
  leave downstream tests broken by stale versions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After `bump-version.js` bumps `package.json` in `merge-dev-to-main.sh` (real
  release mode), the release flow runs the repo's `npm run build` when a `build`
  script exists, and commits the regenerated **tracked** files — so a consumer
  repo's derived version file (e.g. ContextHub `src/version.ts`) matches the bumped
  `package.json` by the time the release completes. Verified by a green version-parity
  test on a consumer repo, or an equivalent unit test of the ship flow using a fixture
  repo.
- [ ] A failing regeneration step does **not** abort the release: a `Warning:`
  message is logged and the release continues, mirroring the CHANGELOG step's
  non-fatal behaviour. Verified by a unit/script test with a failing build script.
- [ ] The mechanism and its trigger are documented: `skill/ship/SKILL.md` and
  `docs/dev/release-process.md` describe that a post-bump, pre-tag build
  regeneration runs on the final merged tree when `scripts.build` exists and is
  non-fatal.
- [ ] A regression test for the ship flow exists (unit test of the regeneration
  step with an injected build command / fixture repo), covering both success and
  failure paths.
- [ ] Existing ship tests pass and the full SorraAgents test suite passes with the
  new changes.

## Constraints

- **Non-fatal regeneration:** a failed or slow build must never block the release
  (operator-confirmed choice); the release path and exit codes stay unchanged.
- **Tracked files only:** commit regenerated files via `git add -u` (or equivalent)
  so build droppings (e.g. `dist/`, new untracked artefacts) are not staged.
- **Trigger sparingly:** only run when a `build` script exists in `package.json`;
  no new mandatory dependencies, no opt-in flags required.
- **Dry-run parity:** `--dry-run` reports the would-be regeneration (like the other
  dry-run echoes) and performs no build/commit.
- Repos that do **not** track their derived version file are out of scope (the
  prerequisite for this fix is that the derived file is committed, as in ContextHub).

## Existing state

- `bump-version.js` reads/writes `package.json` only; the bumped version is
  committed by `merge-dev-to-main.sh` ("Bump version to vX") before merging `dev`.
- The same script already runs a post-bump **non-fatal** regeneration precedent for
  `CHANGELOG.md` (`generate-changelog.js`; `Warning: … continuing with release`),
  which this change mirrors.
- ContextHub tracks `src/version.ts` (`WORKLOG_VERSION`), regenerated by
  `scripts/generate-version.cjs` inside `npm run build`; its parity guard
  `tests/unit/version-parity.test.ts` (commit cf8c09a7) fails fast on drift.
- SorraAgents itself has a no-op `build` script, so this repo is unaffected; the
  step must remain harmless for repos with no real build.

## Desired change

In `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`, after the dev merge (final
tree) and before tagging, run the repo's `npm run build` when `scripts.build`
exists, then stage regenerated tracked files and commit them (e.g. "Regenerate
derived version files for vX"). On build failure, log a warning and continue. Mirror
the CHANGELOG handling for dry-run output. Optionally extract the step into a small
testable Node helper (pattern: `generate-changelog.js` + its test) selected by the
plan step.

## Key Files:

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — add post-merge build + commit step (primary change).
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` — unchanged in the thin case; the derivation trigger may be extracted into a small sibling helper if a unit-test boundary is required.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — document the new step and trigger.
- `docs/dev/release-process.md` — document the new step and trigger (version-bump section, ~line 156).
- New unit test for the regeneration step (fixture repo / injected build command), pattern: `skill/ship/tests/test_generate_changelog_focus.mjs`.

## Related work

- WL-0MV7GV4XW0073FCD — ContextHub triage item for the observed drift (version-parity test failure); consumer-side guard cf8c09a7.
- SA-0MRC71KCR009Y7RL — *Generate CHANGELOG.md during ship release process* (completed) — the post-bump non-fatal regeneration precedent.
- SA-0MPYO85WW006CXPL — *Add version numbering to ship skill for releases* (completed) — introduced the bump step.
- SA-0MRB2FB5X008X4MM, SA-0MQI6MDUP001S8NL — bump-version.js install-path fixes (completed).

### Related work (automated report)

_run: `find_related.py --work-item-id SA-0MV7WAUHZ009UWY2` (full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-SA-0MV7WAUHZ009UWY2.md`)_

Related work items (all completed; context for ship-skill/test-runner behaviour, none conflicting):

- **SA-0MSP7RGX3005HMD0** – *Ship skill scripts unreachable from documented paths* — relevant precedent for changing ship-skill scripts/docs in lockstep.
- **SA-0MSF8KNE3003JDVD** – *Fix node --test directory invocation in test skill runner* — relevant to how the new ship-flow regression test is added under `skill/ship/tests/`.
- **SA-0MS4A7A4Y000L9ED** – *Update cross-references, clean up old files, and verify tests pass* — the cross-reference/documentation-sync pattern.

Repo-file matches returned were generic keyword collisions (e.g. `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`) and are excluded as noise.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Build slowness/failure:** a full build may take minutes or fail for reasons
  unrelated to version derivation — mitigated by non-fatal failure semantics;
  slowness only affects real releases of build-bearing repos.
- **`git add -u` scope:** only already-tracked files are staged; a derived file
  that is newly generated (untracked/gitignored) is not captured — recorded as an
  assumption, not in scope.
- **Commit noise:** regenerated generated-source (e.g. `src/version.ts`) becomes part
  of the release commit; acceptable and desired for parity, and limited to tracked
  files.
- **Scope-creep risk:** generalising to arbitrary derived artefacts or
  multi-repo/CI regeneration is out of scope; record such opportunities as linked
  work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Mechanism — Option A (active regeneration) vs Option B (documentation only)
  vs Hybrid?" — Answer (operator): "A — active regeneration: after bump-version.js
  commits the new package.json version, the release flow runs the repo's
  `npm run build` when a `build` script exists, then commits the regenerated tracked
  files." Source: interactive reply (intake session).
- Q2: "If active regeneration is chosen — if the post-bump build fails, abort the
  release or warn and continue?" — Answer (operator): "B — warn and continue,
  mirroring the CHANGELOG step's non-fatal behaviour." Source: interactive reply
  (intake session). Prior: none. Research: the existing CHANGELOG generation step
  (`Warning: CHANGELOG.md generation failed (continuing with release)`) provides the
  established non-fatal pattern in the same script.
